result.summary: The street environment provides basic sidewalk infrastructure but lacks essential safety features at the intersection, such as marked crosswalks. The presence of utility poles on the walkway and a lack of physical buffers between pedestrians and traffic reduces the overall safety and comfort of the environment.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: The intersection ahead lacks marked crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated or protected space.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the path of the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sidewalks in the foreground and midground

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or planting strip between the sidewalk and the moving traffic lanes.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the street.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a paved sidewalk directly adjacent to the roadway with no buffer. The walkway is significantly obstructed by trash bins and commercial debris, which severely restricts the effective walking width and forces pedestrians toward the curb.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A large collection of trash bins and cardboard boxes occupies more than half of the sidewalk width.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the sidewalk in front of the grey building wall.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the walkway and the active roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: The edge where the sidewalk meets the street surface.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Management and Clearance
interventions.description: Enforce regulations regarding the storage of trash and commercial goods to maintain a clear pedestrian through-zone.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install a furniture zone or planting strip to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by narrow sidewalks with significant obstructions from debris on the left side. The street lacks basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks, lane markings, or traffic calming measures, creating a shared space with vehicles that lacks clear pedestrian priority.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Piles of boxes and debris on the left sidewalk force pedestrians to walk in the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: The absence of marked crosswalks at visible points increases risk for pedestrians crossing the street.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clearing Program
interventions.description: Implement regular enforcement and clearing of sidewalks to ensure they remain passable for all users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions at corners to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians and shorten crossing distances.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly deficient, lacking a paved sidewalk, curbing, or any form of separation from vehicular traffic. Pedestrians are forced to navigate a narrow, unpaved shoulder obstructed by overgrown vegetation, utility poles, and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: Complete absence of a dedicated pedestrian walkway, forcing people into the roadway or onto an uneven shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and midground along the road edge

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A silver van is parked on the shoulder, forcing pedestrians to walk further into the travel lane and blocking sightlines.

hazards.name: Physical Obstructions on Shoulder
hazards.description: Utility poles and overgrown weeds further restrict the usable space on the unpaved shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the fence line

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb and Gutter
interventions.description: Install a raised curb to physically separate the pedestrian zone from the vehicle travel lane and manage drainage.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety for those walking at night.
